newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking pulls down Bombay shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pulls down Bombay shares at close.

text.p: Sharp intra-day gains recorded by Bombay shares on Wednesday were wiped out by close of trade on a late bout of profit-taking by speculators, traders said.
The top 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rallied 67.70 points, or 2.3 percent, to an intra-day high of 3,051.72 before dropping to close at 2,997.88 provisional.
"The market's taken a breather... the brake has been put on the sharp spurt in prices," said a dealer at a local firm.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 7.21 points, or 0.85 percent, to end at a provisional 858.21.

Analysts see the depressed market bottoming out after discounting a series of negative factors, such as an economic slowdown, poor first-half company results and the coalition government's inability to push through liberalisation measures.
"The selling frenzy in the recent past was the result of all-round pessimism ...with valuations counting for little," said Ramnath Iyer, strategist at Peregrine Capital.
Bombay stocks which fell to a three-year low of 2,713.12 on December 4, have gained about 10.5 percent from that level.
Some dealers said news that former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao had been asked to quit as chief of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) might help improve sentiment.
The technical rally, however, might weaken said Mehmood Khan, technical analyst at Times Guaranty Financial Ltd.
"The uptrend seems to be losing momentum day by day...the rally may falter," Khan said.
ACC rose 12.50 rupees to 1,128.50, Bajaj Auto 4.50 to 797.0, Glaxo 12.75 to 248.50 and Tata Chemicals 4.50 to 168.0.
Reliance and SBI were unchanged at 194.25 and 218.50 rupees.
